title: Register
description: One table per guarantee, keyed by id, plus an optional `corpus` header table. This schema is necessary and not sufficient: the parser also requires a budget of at least ceil(p95 × 1.5), a teardown wherever holds is non-empty, a file carrying the suffix the runner collects, one row expecting failure in every tier that holds rows, and every such tier triggered and proven by the pipeline.

version.description: The contract version this schema is published under. A register names it in `corpus.contract` and a probe in `contract`; a document naming another version is refused rather than read as this one.

exitCodes.description: What a run's exit code means. `green` and `red` are verdicts read from the report the run wrote, never from the runner's own exit code; `refused` is the scheduler declining to judge — a register, a report or a probe it could not read, a report that is not this run's, a run in which nothing executed. Carried here because the register is the document every implementation reads first.

limits.description: The numbers the parser and the scheduler hold a register to: per-tier ceilings in seconds, the deadline on everything outside the measured window, and the budget rule — the floor, the headroom, the hard-kill multiplier, how many measured windows a budget is set from and the p95 estimator over them, nearest rank. A tier absent from `ceilings` has none.

contract.description: The contract version the register is written against; any other is refused. Absent — no header, or a header without it — the register is written against the default, the version at which the header did not exist, and never against the current one.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, opening on a letter or a digit; a directory name and half a container name before it is anything else. `corpus` is reserved for the register's header and `reports` for the lifted run reports.

kind.description: What sort of fact the row pins. The kinds in `$defs/pooledKinds` run as a pool; every other kind runs one at a time after the pool drains, as does any row that declares `holds`.

pooledKinds.description: The kinds whose rows share the machine, running as a pool at its concurrency. A row of any other kind, and a row of these that declares `holds`, runs alone after the pool drains: a budget measured beside other containers is not the budget, and a held resource is one another row could contend for. Carried as data so an implementation reads the partition from the file rather than from prose.

tier.description: The earliest moment the thing the row pins could have changed, demoted only as its cost demands.

isolation.description: What the measured run may reach. `image-net` keeps the image and drops only the network wall.

expect.description: `fail` marks the row designed to fail; a tier is green only once it has been seen to fail.

image.description: The image the run is admissible in, pinned by digest and never by tag.

file.description: The test file, relative to the corpus directory and inside it, on one line. Which suffix a runner collects is that runner's rule, so the parser holds the file to the suffix its caller names and the schema does not.

recipes.description: Task-face recipe names, each run in order.

class.description: A machine class, never a hostname.

p95.description: The measurement the budget came from, in seconds.

budget.description: Seconds: the p95 rounded to a tenth, times 1.5, rounded up, and never below 10. The hard kill is 3 times this.

select.description: The title of the entry's suite, or of its one test, as the host runner joins titles with single spaces; matched from the start of the full title and never as a pattern, so what the row writes is what the runner selects.

holds.description: Resources the entry keeps beyond its own container. Naming one obliges a teardown.
